problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a nutrient‑runoff mitigation strategy to lower total nitrogen discharge from several agricultural drainage points. Initially, no treatment practices are in place.

The characteristics of each drainage point are as follows:
* For Field 1, the leaching coefficient is 0.835, and the cultivated area is 247.356 units.
* For Field 2, the leaching coefficient is 1.693, and the cultivated area is 194.497 units.
* For Field 3, the leaching coefficient is 1.081, and the cultivated area is 79.457 units.
* For Field 4, the leaching coefficient is 2.648, and the cultivated area is 51.799 units.
* For Field 5, the leaching coefficient is 1.208, and the cultivated area is 213.637 units.
* For Field 6, the leaching coefficient is 2.692, and the cultivated area is 221.942 units.
* For Field 7, the leaching coefficient is 1.522, and the cultivated area is 128.975 units.
* For Field 8, the leaching coefficient is 0.973, and the cultivated area is 140.567 units.
* For Field 9, the leaching coefficient is 2.273, and the cultivated area is 88.695 units.

To reduce runoff, several best‑management practices (BMPs) can be adopted, each with a specific nitrogen‑removal effectiveness:
* Practice A achieves a 38% reduction
* Practice B achieves a 70% reduction
* Practice C achieves a 22% reduction
* Practice D achieves a 56% reduction
* Practice E achieves a 61% reduction
* Practice F achieves a 68% reduction
* Practice G achieves a 36% reduction
* Practice H achieves a 30% reduction
* Practice I achieves a 57% reduction

Implementing a practice on a field incurs an extra expense per unit of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all field–practice combinations is as follows:

| Field \ Practice | Practice A | Practice B | Practice C | Practice D | Practice E | Practice F | Practice G | Practice H | Practice I |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Field 1 | 158.92 | 101.669 | 80.34 | 115.433 | 58.218 | 68.264 | 75.428 | 144.044 | 149.799 |
| Field 2 | 172.45 | 135.264 | 152.085 | 94.853 | 142.869 | 40.741 | 50.747 | 86.107 | 74.303 |
| Field 3 | 114.609 | 142.441 | 144.29 | 40.54 | 193.268 | 11.005 | 27.307 | 37.612 | 185.914 |
| Field 4 | 92.722 | 22.175 | 52.136 | 25.208 | 17.174 | 83.022 | 197.045 | 126.653 | 108.991 |
| Field 5 | 145.205 | 123.52 | 189.686 | 165.843 | 131.655 | 93.405 | 48.324 | 134.808 | 162.743 |
| Field 6 | 64.341 | 16.386 | 123.908 | 108.005 | 54.017 | 42.202 | 16.852 | 55.459 | 10.055 |
| Field 7 | 39.915 | 199.395 | 158.138 | 77.094 | 85.077 | 121.355 | 108.371 | 150.016 | 23.037 |
| Field 8 | 27.132 | 64.054 | 167.655 | 183.852 | 76.138 | 193.025 | 62.536 | 125.209 | 46.96 |
| Field 9 | 186.646 | 119.232 | 59.61 | 87.356 | 30.228 | 23.753 | 65.908 | 189.933 | 162.559 |

The decision involves selecting which practices to apply to each drainage point (multiple practices may be combined on the same field), and a field may also remain partially untreated if needed. The objective is to guarantee that the overall nitrogen discharge is lowered by at least a fraction P = 0.678 of the baseline load, while minimizing the total implementation cost.
